record.original_question: Let (Omega, mu) be a sigma-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L2(Omega), let a: V x V -> C be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, let -A generate the associated bounded analytic semigroup (T(t)) on L2(Omega), and assume that (T(t)) is L-infinity-bounded. Characterize exactly when there exists a function g in L-infinity(Omega) with g > 0 mu-almost everywhere and 1/g in L-infinity(Omega) such that ||g T(t)f||_infinity <= ||g f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega) and all t >= 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space and let $V$ be a dense subspace of $L^2(\Omega)$. Let $a\colon V\times V\to\mathbb{C}$ be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, and let $-A$ be the associated operator that generates a bounded analytic semigroup $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ on $L^2(\Omega)$. Assume that $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ is $L^\infty$-bounded, in the sense that there exists $M\ge 0$ with $\|T(t)f\|_\infty \le M\|f\|_\infty$ for all $f\in L^2(\Omega)\cap L^\infty(\Omega)$ and all $t\ge 0$.

Give a necessary and sufficient condition (in terms of the form $a$, the operator $A$, or the semigroup $(T(t))$) for the existence of a function $g\in L^\infty(\Omega)$ with $g>0$ $\mu$-almost everywhere and $1/g\in L^\infty(\Omega)$ such that
$$\|g\,T(t)f\|_\infty \;\le\; \|g\,f\|_\infty$$
for every $f\in L^2(\Omega)\cap L^\infty(\Omega)$ and every $t\ge 0$.
